The mysterious “ribonucleoprotein particle” that recognizes a nascent polypeptide, tells it to “pause,” and then “shows it in” so it can “get some sugar” is the Signal Recognition Particle (SRP).

• SRP is a ribonucleoprotein.  
• When SRP binds the emerging signal peptide on a growing chain, it halts (pauses) translation.  
• SRP brings the ribosome–nascent-chain complex to the SRP receptor on the rough ER membrane; translation then resumes with the peptide threaded into/through the ER.  
• In the ER lumen the protein receives N-linked oligosaccharide chains (“some sugar”).  
• From the ER, the polypeptide continues through the secretory pathway (ER → Golgi → vesicle) to be released outside the cell.

Thus they first meet in the cytosol, and the chain’s ultimate destination is the extracellular space.

Answer: C
